questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am studying public health and Norway is a country where health care has a high priority. Norway is to some extend similar to Denmark in the way they organize health care, but there are also some differences. I thought it would be interesting to go to Oslo University, because they offer some very interesting courses, that I am not able to take in Denmark. Furthermore I thought it was interesting to get another perspective on the subject of public health that I could take with me back to Denmark in my further studies and career. I believe that my stay in Oslo has provided me with that. Additionally I really like to be in the nature, thus the norwegian nature and the opportunity to experience that was also a crucial reason for choosing Oslo as my study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought the courses were very relevant and interesting. Furthermore I got some new friends and I generally really enjoyed being here.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was quite easy to find the information that I needed to know upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended an online introduction to Norway, but that was more to the culture and what to expect. I also attended a meeting with the international coordinator at UIO when I arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would have liked to have a more thorough introduction where I would also meet more (exchange)students from the university

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I used the webpage
finn.no
and there were several housing opportunities there, but the options here are quite expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Know that it's quite expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have liked to live at campus, if it was possible to get a housing that was furnished. I was offered an unfurnished room and I find it quite expensive to buy a bed, desk and so on to only be here for 6 months.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was in contact with an international coordinator at UIO, who also signed my online learning agreement. When he saw on the learning agreement which courses I wanted to register for he made sure that I was signed up for those. There was one course which was outside the faculty and for that course I needed to contact the course leader and the other faculty in order to sign up, but that was also rather straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: See the above description.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was just one course that wasn't available afterall. But other than that I could register for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take contact to the international coordinator/person in charge of the online learning agreement, they are happy to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All the courses I took were on a masters level, but I experienced that some of the courses had a somewhat lower level than what I am used to at University of Copenhagen. Thus, that was a bit disappointing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In some courses the teaching style was quite similar. I had three courses that lasteded to two weeks each. This is very different from what I have experienced before. I got used to these short courses, but I think I learn more from having the course spread out over a longer period. Further I had a few courses where the academic level was lower compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HELSEF4405 - Kjønn, kropp og medikalisering
PSY4116 - Sentrale temaer i anvendt helsepsykologi
HMAN4210 - Leadership, Management and Organization Development
INTHE4113 - Introduction to Medical Anthropology: Key Concepts and Perspectives
HELSEF4511 - Digitalisering, samhandling og innovasjon

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: HELSEF4405 - Kjønn, kropp og medikalisering. I really liked this course. But I would also recommend introduction to medical anthropology

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I encountered any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything was more expensive than I expected. Norway is just a very expensive country to live in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was e.g. a weekend course in cross-country skiing that I participated in. Further it was possible to students to be a member of a sportsclub at a reasonable price. There were not too many social activities which was a shame.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I thought it was a lot of fun to attend the cross country skiing course. I really wanted to learn it and it was also a fun way to meet some new people. I know that they make more sports activities like that and I really like that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of weekends in the winter going cross country skiing. It's possible to do it just outside of Oslo which is really nice and so much fun. When the weather became better I really enjoyed going on shorter as well as longer trips to the nature to hike and experience the nature. Furthermore Oslo is a nice city with lots of museums and nice neighborhoods to explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I think there are a lot of similarities between Denmark and Norway.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I got a few local friends because I had courses in Norwegian. I would say that this is a good way to meet some local people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience any very challenging differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate that Norway offer so many opportunities to be outdoors. And it's great to experience how so many Norwegians also use the outdoors.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that everything is very expensive. If it wasn't for the grands that I was lucky to receive I would have had a hard time to make it work economically. Know that it takes some time to adjust both to "normal life", but also to the new university and new courses, even if the culture and university is quite similar to your own. And I would very much recommend going to Norway if you enjoy being outdoors - they have a lot of things to offer here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If it's possible try and see if you can attend an introduction week even if it isn't offered at your specific study. I know people who could then attend an introduction week of another study/faculty. Just contact the international coordinator and see if they can help you find a solution.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed getting to know the small differences between the norwegian and the danish culture. Those are things that I wouldn't have noticed if I was just here on a short visit. Furthermore I really enjoyed most of the courses that I was able to take here. That provided me with new knowledge and new perspectives, that I don't think I could've gotten in Denmark. I also really enjoyed being able to experience the beautiful nature of Norway!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it was a challenge to get local friends. I had hoped to get more local friends, but I mainly became friends with other international students.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
